  "summary": "Dijkstra argues that program text should keep a close correspondence with the dynamic process, using textual and dynamic indices to describe process progress. He claims the unrestricted go to destroys the helpful coordinate system and should be eliminated from higher-level languages.",
  "digest": "The article begins with the observation that programmer quality decreases as go to density increases. Dijkstra distinguishes static program text from the dynamic process and stresses that programmers have limited ability to visualize processes evolving in time. He develops textual indices for straight-line, conditional, alternative, choice, and conditional-expression programs; then adds procedures and repetition clauses, leading to mixed sequences of textual and dynamic indices. These coordinates are independent of programmer control. He argues that variables are meaningful only relative to process progress, and unrestricted go to prevents a meaningful set of coordinates. Although a normalized clock can uniquely describe progress, it is unhelpful. He concludes that go to is too primitive and that proposed clauses should preserve a programmer-independent coordinate system.",
